try.title: Five bonds on one carbon.
try.why: The arrow makes a new O–C bond, but that carbon already has four bonds. Unless a second arrow breaks the C–Cl bond and sends that pair to chlorine, the carbon would hold five bonds. Hydroxide does have lone pairs, and the tail belongs on them.

try.title: One sixteenth of the flow.
try.why: Resistance depends on 1 ÷ radius to the fourth power. Halving the radius makes the radius to the fourth power (½)⁴ = 1/16 as large, so resistance becomes 16 times larger. With ΔP unchanged, F = ΔP / R becomes 1/16 of the original.

sample.q: On hot days, African elephants flap their very large, thin ears, which are full of blood vessels. How do the ears help the elephant?
opts: They add a lot of surface for little volume, so heat leaves the blood faster.
They make the elephant look larger to predators, so it can rest more and use less oxygen per gram.
They store extra water, which the elephant draws on to keep its blood cool on hot days.
They lower the elephant's volume, which lowers its body temperature.
